### cavity3d

In this setup, the lid-driven velocity is treated as a random variable, uniformly distributed over the interval $\mathcal{U}[0.9, 1.1]$, representing $\pm 10\%$ uncertainty around the nominal value.

Uncertain input distributions can be defined using utility functions such as `uniform()` or `normal()`. For example:

```{.cpp}
// Define a uniform distribution in the range [0.8 * u0 ... 1.2 * u0]
auto dist = uniform(0.8 * u0, 1.2 * u0);

// Alternatively, define a normal distribution with mean u0 and standard deviation 0.1
auto dist = normal(u0, 0.1);
```

Once the distribution is defined, the sampling method is selected through the `UncertaintyQuantification` interface.
Two modes are supported.

**(1) Monte Carlo sampling** draws random samples from the distribution and computes statistics such as the mean and variance:

```{.cpp}
UncertaintyQuantification<T> uq(UQMethod::MonteCarlo);
unsigned int seed = 123456; // fixed seed for reproducibility
uq.initializeMonteCarlo(nq, dist, seed);
```

The combination of Monte Carlo methods and LBM was further studied in [@zhong2024stochastic; @simonis:23b; @simonis2024computing] and used for large-scale production of training data for generative diffusion models in [@molinaro2025generative].

**(2) The stochastic collocation method** employs generalized polynomial chaos (GPC) with deterministic quadrature sampling for spectral convergence in smooth problems:

```{.cpp}
// Generalized Polynomial Chaos (gPC) with order and quadrature
UncertaintyQuantification<T> uq(UQMethod::GPC);
uq.initializeGPC(orderGPC, nqPerDim, dist);
```

Here `orderGPC` denotes the order of the GPC expansion, `nqPerDim` denotes the number of quadrature points in each uncertain input dimension, and `dist` denotes a random distribution.

After initialization, sampling points can be retrieved via:

```{.cpp}
auto samples = uq.getSamplingPoints();
```

Once the simulations for all generated samples are completed, statistical postprocessing can be applied to any quantity of interest.
For example, to compute and export the mean and standard deviation of the velocity field:

```{.cpp}
computeMeanAndStdAndWriteVTI<T, DESCRIPTOR>(
  uq, foldPath, "cavity2d", "physVelocity",
  superGeometry, materials
);
```

Simulation results -- such as the mean and standard deviation of the velocity -- can be visualized to assess the influence of parametric uncertainty on flow behavior (see @fig-uqCavity-3d).

::: {#fig-uqCavity-3d layout-ncol=2}

![Mean $\bar{|\mathbf{u}|}$.](/examples/uncertaintyQuantification/cavity2d/doc/fig/uqCavityMean.png){#fig-uqCavityMean-3d}

![Standard deviation $\sigma(|\mathbf{u}|)$.](/examples/uncertaintyQuantification/cavity2d/doc/fig/uqCavityStd.png){#fig-uqCavityStd-3d}

Mean and standard deviation of the velocity magnitude, computed using the stochastic collocation method with a second-order polynomial expansion and five quadrature points.

:::
